name: The Litany Sea
tagline: A war over the nature of truth, fought with salt and brine on the corpse of a god, with a clock everyone can hear.
premise: When the leviathan-deity Veyl was slain in the deep past, it did not bleed — it wept, and its grief filled the basin of the world to become the Litany Sea, an ocean of brine in which every drop held a remembered moment. Now the Sea is dying: the rust-red sun has not set in living memory, and the brine is evaporating, receding thigh-deep then ankle-deep then gone, crystallizing as it goes into salt-glass that fossilizes real history — each crystal a moment you can re-live, sell, edit, set forever, or shatter so that it never happened at all. Across this drying flat wade the memory-archivists, rival orders who have realized that whichever version of the past is still crystallized when the…
twist: The leviathan-deity Veyl is not dead — it is grieving, and the Litany Sea is not its corpse but its open, weeping wound, still dreaming. Every crystal is a tear it has not finished crying, and the "history" the archivists fight to fix or erase is in fact Veyl actively re-remembering its own life as it dies, which is why the salt-dead keep rising: they are the god flinching at moments it cannot let go. The brine is not evaporating from heat — it is being wept out, and when the last pool dries,…

mechanics.name: The Long Toll (the living, audible clock)
mechanics.concept: The receding brine is a shared doomsday clock every faction reads identically. The Sea is genuinely alive during play: each round the tide marker advances one step on a fixed track audible as the 'Toll,' and the entire board physically transforms — Brine-deep zones recede to Dry, exposing crystals;…

mechanics.name: Custody & Collateral (capture WITHOUT breaking)
mechanics.concept: Crystals are fragile, irreplaceable, lore-bearing OBJECTS, not abstract tokens. The core tension is seizing or protecting a specific thing without shattering it in the crossfire — collateral damage as the central dilemma. You cannot win by destroying the board; you win by having intact, controlled…

mechanics.name: The Dreaming Grief (re-dreaming & board corruption)
mechanics.concept: Veyl's grief still dreams, and the salt-dead — Reliquiae, ghosts who exist only while their crystal stays solid — are the crisis given a face.
